text: dsh-memory-chain 是面向 DSH 的本地记忆插件，通过 system prompt 区段和七个工具提供文档库、跨会话桥接、带衰减权重的长期记忆、产物索引及自我叙述。它可保存并检索长文档、记录或撤销稳定事实，在新会话提示近期对话，并把记忆内容按权重呈现。适合希望 DSH 延续上下文、留存资料并控制提示词记忆预算的用户。插件默认把数据写入本地 DSH_HOME/memory；无需 API key。

dsh-memory-chain adds persistent memory to DSH with prompt sections and tools: a local document library, session bridge, weighted notes, artifact index, and self-narrative. Users can search saved documents and retain facts across sessions. Data is stored locally by default; no API key is needed.
想让 DSH 在新会话里接上上一段对话的重点。
我需要把长文档保存在本机，需要时再按关键词找出来。
Help me keep durable notes available across separate DSH conversations.
dsh-memory-chain 的功能「本地文档库」：将长内容保存为 Markdown 文档，并按标题、标签或关键词搜索；搜索返回标题、片段和路径，工具可按 id 分页读取正文。
dsh-memory-chain 的功能「跨会话记忆」：记录带权重的长期事实，并在后续提示词中呈现当前优先条目；也可撤销并归档旧记忆。
dsh-memory-chain 使用前须知：设置 Git remote 后，记忆目录会通过 Git pull/push 同步到该远端。（见 lib/sync.js:27-35、lib/sync.js:65-70）

dsh-memory-chain README · dsh-memory-chain：Five-layer memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): **opening a new conversation shouldn't feel like meeting a stranger.**

Zero dependencies, no patches to the DSH install, everything on local files. It exists to answer one question — context windows are expensive, so why store "remembering" and "recalling" in the same place?

English | [中文说明](README.zh.md)

dsh-memory-chain README · The five layers：| Layer | What is stored | Cost per request |
|---|---|---|
| **L0 Library** | Bodies on disk in `L0/docs/<id>.md`, index in `L0/index.json` | Titles + ids of the 6 newest, ≤420 chars |
| **L1 Bridge** | The last 4 messages of the previous session, read from the session event log | ≤320 chars, and only in the first turns of a new session |
| **L2 Recall** | Ebbinghaus-weighted entries | Top 12 by weight, ≤1100 chars |
| **L3 Artifacts** | Documents tagged `artifact:*` | 5 newest, ≤320 chars, owner switch |
| **L4 Self-note** | What the model writes about itself, rolling window | 24 entries / 3600 chars |
dsh-memory-chain README · The five layers：All five are system-prompt sections, re-evaluated on every assembly. Nothing is appended to the message history.

dsh-memory-chain README · Measured cost：Numbers from one machine (the host estimates 4 chars/token; CJK text is denser in practice):

- Tool schemas, all 7: 2331 chars ≈ **583 tokens per request**
- The four cards, with 2 documents and 1 artifact in the library: **338 chars ≈ 85 tokens**
- A 1100-character artifact costs **34 tokens** in context; its body stays on disk

dsh-memory-chain README · Measured cost：Tool schemas are a permanent tax, which is why L3 adds **no new tool** — it reuses `memory_search(tag:"artifact")` and only pays for one extra `tag` field (+17 tokens).

dsh-memory-chain README · Install：Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2`.

```bash
dsh-memory-chain README · from a local checkout：dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-memory-chain

dsh-memory-chain README · or straight from git：dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/doresu/dsh-memory-chain.git
```

The plugin manager adds the package to the profile's `bundles` — no manual patch editing. Then **restart the engine**.

Check `~/.dsh/memory/state.json`:json
{ "status": "active", "sections": 5, "tools": 7 }
```

A new conversation should show a `## 原文库` section once it is live.

Manual install without the package manager: see [`examples/cordis.patch.yml`](examples/cordis.patch.yml).

dsh-memory-chain README · Files：```
$DSH_HOME/memory/
  L1/bridge.json      tail of the previous conversation
  L0/index.json       document index
  L0/docs/<id>.md     document bodies

dsh-memory-chain README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `memory_write_doc` | Persist a document; same title updates in place, id stays |
| `memory_search` | Keyword search returning snippets and paths, **never full text**; optional `tag` |
| `memory_read_doc` | Read a body by id, pageable |
| `memory_note` | Record a durable fact; same key merges, raises weight, lengthens half-life |
| `memory_forget` | Retract a fact (archived, not deleted) |
| `selfnote_append` | Append a self-narrative entry |
| `selfnote_rewrite` | Rewrite the whole window; the old version is archived first |

dsh-memory-chain README · Design notes：- **Sections, not messages.** Sections are re-evaluated every assembly and cost no history. `interpolate: false` keeps `{{…}}` inside memory text from being read as template variables.
- **Weights are bucketed to 0.05 before hashing.** Decay is continuous, but the prompt only reorders when a value crosses a bucket — otherwise the prefix cache is invalidated every turn.
- **Assembly happens before `agent/pre-step`.** `preStep()` calls `assemble()` first and only then dispatches the waterfall, so anything a section needs must come from the assembly context (`text(context)` receives `{ agent, scope, signal }`) — not from state written by the hook.
- **`agent/pre-step` carries a delta, not history.** Its `messages` are the inbox claim for that step — at step 1 that is just the incoming user message. Anything that needs conversation context must read `agent.session.log`, whose events also include injected user messages (`time-context`, `skill-catalog`, …) that must be filtered out by `source.kind`.
- **L1 is truncation, not summarisation.** A summary would cost an extra model call and would drift; truncation is free, faithful, and merely unpolished

dsh-memory-chain README · Known limits：- **No semantic search.** L0 matches substrings; phrasing too far from the original wording will miss. This is measured rather than assumed: every zero-result search is appended to `L0/misses.jsonl`, and `node scripts/misses.mjs` summarises it. If a month of misses stays in the single digits, embeddings are a solution without a problem. Embeddings mean a dependency and a network hop — a bad trade on a phone.
- **Code changes need an engine restart.** The host caches ES modules. During development you can bust it with `file://…?v=2`, but only a recomposition actually reloads.
- **The owner switch only hides a card**, it is not password-grade isolation. Per-session isolation would mean registering tools in an agent scope.
- **No cross-process locking.** Two processes writing the same JSON can lose an update; fine for a single host.
- `importance` on L2 is filled in by the model, not a calibrated parameter.
- Recall matching is 4-gram lexical overlap: it misses paraphrases ("memory decay" vs "forgetting curve") and can fire on a generic phrase. The boost is deliberately small so a false positive costs little.

dsh-memory-chain README · Development：```bash
node test/store.test.mjs        # 35 tests, pure functions, no DSH needed
node test/integration.mjs      # boots a throwaway DSH and checks the plugin really activates
node scripts/misses.mjs        # summarises searches that returned nothing
```
